newsitem.title: GERMANY: HOECHST SAYS INCOME FALLS, SEES LOWER 1997 EARNINGS.
newsitem.headline: HOECHST SAYS INCOME FALLS, SEES LOWER 1997 EARNINGS.

text.p: German chemical giant Hoechst AG Wednesday reported a 54 percent decline in pre-tax profits in the first half of 1997 and said its full-year net income would trail 1996, when income from one-time items bolstered its bottom line.
But Hoechst said it still expected a slight rise in full-year operating profits compared with 1996 after extraordinary gains from the sale of companies and stock were stripped out.

Net income declined to 2 billion marks ($1.1 billion) in the first half of this year, from 4.32 billion marks ($2.35 billion) in the comparable year-ago period. The results were largely in line with analysts' expectations.

"We are optimistic that operating profit for the full year will increase slightly on a comparable basis," the company said in a statement. "Since the high level of extraordinary gains on the sale of companies and shareholdings in 1996 will not be incurred in 1997, net income will be lower."

Hoechst's operating profits fell 18 percent to 2.27 billion marks ($1.23 billion) in the first half of 1997 from 2.775 billion marks ($1.51 billion) in the same period last year. Excluding special items, operating profit rose by 7 percent, the company said, aided by strength on the dollar vs. the mark.
Sales at Hoechst in the first half totaled 27.886 billion marks ($15.2 billion) compared with 26.091 billion marks ($14.2 billion) in the same period of 1996.
Hoechst is one of Germany's big three chemical companies, along with Bayer AG and BASF AG.
